metaTitle: Pallet Sizes Chart: 48×40 and Common Pallet Dimensions — AGL Pallet
metaDescription: A pallet size chart with the 48×40 GMA footprint, common North American sizes by industry, ISO and European sizes, and how pallet size affects trailer and container fit.

sections.heading: How pallet sizes are written
paragraphs: In North America, pallet sizes are written length × width in inches, with the stringer length first. A 48 × 40 pallet has 48-inch stringers and 40-inch deckboards. Outside North America, sizes are usually given in millimeters, and the order convention varies, so confirm which dimension is which before quoting.
Height is a separate figure. Most wood pallets fall around 5 to 6.5 inches tall, depending on board thickness and stringer or block height, and height matters for trailer cube and stacking.

sections.heading: Common North American pallet sizes
paragraphs: The 48 × 40 GMA footprint is the most common size in North America by a wide margin. Other sizes persist because they fit a specific product, container, or door.

table.caption: Common North American pallet sizes and typical industries
rows: Grocery, consumer goods, and most general freight
table.note: Industry associations are commonly cited in industry summaries (see the [Wikipedia "Pallet" article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallet), which draws on pallet-industry sources). They describe typical use, not rules. Your receiver's requirement always wins.

sections.heading: ISO and international sizes
paragraphs: [ISO 6780](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#iso:std:iso:6780:ed-2:v1:en) lists a small set of principal pallet dimensions for intercontinental handling. The 48 × 40 inch footprint (1219 × 1016 mm) is one of them. The others are metric sizes used in Europe, Asia, and Australia.

table.caption: Principal international pallet sizes
table.note: Metric-to-inch conversions are rounded. Confirm exact dimensions and tolerances in the current edition of ISO 6780 before specifying for a container program.

after: The square Australian size is a known point of disagreement. The Australian standard pallet and pooled pallets such as [CHEP's Australian standard](https://www.chep.com/us/en/products/pallets/standard-pallet-sizes) measure 1165 × 1165 mm, and many summaries list that as the ISO square size. Other references list 1140 × 1140 mm for ISO 6780. The two are not interchangeable in a tight container load, so if a lane depends on the square size, check the standard's current text and the receiver's actual pallet, not a secondary chart.

sections.heading: How size affects trailer and container fit
paragraphs: A 48 × 40 pallet loads two across in a standard North American dry van, either with the 40-inch side across the trailer (straight) or the 48-inch side across (turned). Turning pallets usually fits more positions on the floor. For counts by trailer length, see [pallets per truckload](/resources/pallets-per-truckload/).

ISO shipping containers were not designed around the 48 × 40 footprint, so every pallet size leaves some floor space unused in a container. Metric sizes such as 1200 × 1000 and 1200 × 800 are common in lanes that start or end in Europe and Asia; confirm the receiving country's handling equipment before choosing.

sections.heading: Choosing a size
list: Start from the receiver: many retailers and distributors specify the footprint.
Keep product within the pallet edge; overhang crushes cartons.
Check racking beam spacing and conveyor widths at both ends.
Check trailer or container fit for the lane, including height.
If no standard size fits the product, a custom size is often cheaper than damage. See [custom and engineered pallets](/custom-engineered/).
after: A downloadable PDF of this chart is planned; the HTML tables above are the reference version and are free to use with a link back.

items.question: What is the standard pallet size in the US?
answer: The most common pallet size in the United States is 48 × 40 inches, often called the GMA pallet. It is also one of the sizes listed in ISO 6780. Many other sizes are in regular use, usually because a product, container, or receiver calls for them.

items.question: Is the ISO square pallet 1140 × 1140 or 1165 × 1165 mm?
answer: References disagree. The Australian standard pallet, including pooled pallets, is 1165 × 1165 mm, and many summaries list that as the ISO square size, while other references list 1140 × 1140 mm. Check the current edition of ISO 6780 and the receiver's actual pallet before specifying.
